newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm as cold takes grip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm as cold takes grip.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. firmed Tuesday as cold weather took hold of the region after unseasonably mild temperatures last week.
"They are inching their way up," said a New York power trader.
Outlook for the rest of the week showed readings would peak 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit and bottom in the teens to 20s with increasing winds and possibility of snow this weekend.
Higher costs for generation fuel, primarily natural gas, also supported prices today, market sources said.
Swing natural gas prices at the New York City gate jumped to $4.50-$4.90 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) from Monday's $4.00.
But on the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures tumbled 27.6 cents/mmBtu to $3.380 on profit-taking after Monday's sharp rise.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Wednesday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) jumped to $25.50-$27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Monday's $23.50-$25.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP rose to $16.00-$16.50 from $15.00-$16.00 Monday.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday was quoted at $27.50-$31.00/MWh, up from Monday's $27.00-30.00.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Wednesday were notionally assessed $19.50-$22.50, compared with a quote of $19.00-$22.00 Monday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border stayed in a $31.00-$34.00/MWh range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was remained at $21.00-$23.00.
